result.proposed_fix: Replace the flat value set with structured tokens. (1) In numbers(), before the plain-number pass, recognise compound numerals as single ordered literals: ISO dates \d{4}-\d{1,2}-\d{1,2} and slash/dash dates \d{1,2}[/-]\d{1,2}[/-]\d{2,4} normalised to one canonical form (keep the written order for ambiguous D/M; never sort); times \d{1,2}:\d{2}(:\d{2})?; ratios and fractions a:b and a/b; ranges a-b, a–b and 'a to b' / 'from a to b' as ordered pairs; month-name dates read as one value. (2) Keep the subset test, but over these ordered compound tokens, so a swap is a different token and a range never matches its reversed form. (3) In find_conflicts, do not let subset suppression hide a pair whose compound tokens differ. (4) Add class-level parametrised regressions (every separator in [-, /, :, –, 'to'] x swap/reorder) for verify and find_conflicts, plus the existing R1/R4/R5 cases. (5) Correct W1_QUALIFICATION.md AC10/AC11 with a recorded correction, and list number-to-referent binding (multi-value sentences) as a carried lexical limitation alongside L-W1-1.
result.root_cause: uri_web/evaluate.py reduces each sentence to an unordered, flat set of numeric tokens (numbers(), evaluate.py:94-107), and both W1-AC10 and W1-AC11 then compare by set subset: synthesize.verify keeps a claim if claim_nums <= best_sentence_nums (synthesize.py:100) and find_conflicts suppresses any pair where na<=nb or nb<=na (evaluate.py:194). The tokenizer (_NUMBER num group, evaluate.py:24) only joins digits across ',', '.' and space before a 3-digit group, so every compound numeral using '-', '/', ':' or 'to' (ISO/slash dates, ranges, ratios, times, fractions) is split into components, and set semantics then discard order and role. Swapped or reordered compound values therefore produce identical sets: verify KEEPS the unsupported claim and find_conflicts reports 0 conflicts. Only dotted dates work, because _read keeps '\d+(\.\d+)+' as one literal. The same model also cannot bind a number to its referent: source '5% in 2025 and 10% in 2026' supports claim '10% in 2025'.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: Only repairs 1, 4 and 5 touched the number code; repairs 2 (627f6b9) and 3 (16155129) changed only redaction. Each of the three patched the _NUMBER regex for the exact surface forms the reviewer listed: 16f75d8 changed the lookbehind from (?<![\w.]) to (?<!\d) and tested only Rs./approx./No.; 52e852d added scale and unit suffixes; 08a4569 added Indian/space grouping, sign and an UNREADABLE marker for ',', '.' and space only. None changed the set/subset comparison or the fact that unhandled separators split a numeral into order-free fragments, and every regression test reused the reviewer's examples rather than covering the class, so each review round found a new instance (R1-01 -> R4-02 -> R5-01 -> R6-01). W1_QUALIFICATION.md:22-23 was updated to MET after each repair, and section 4 lists no date or compound-numeral residual, although AC11 explicitly names 'different number/date'.
